scope: Pinned primary-source call graph inspection; not target clipboard runtime acceptance
call_graph: C glfwGetClipboardString/glfwSetClipboardString delegate to the active platform implementation.
C _glfwInputError stores code/description in C thread-local error state (or pre-init state) before invoking the error callback.
Go goErrorCB writes its own buffered Go channel; flushErrors/fetchError drain that channel only.
Go GetClipboardString accepts absent-format errors; acceptError/panicError can log a platform error and return success. They do not call C glfwGetError.
Go GetError calls C glfwGetError, which reads and clears the separate C error code; its Go channel cleanup is independent.

Vellum clears stale C state before an operation, then reads its current-operation error on the same pinned main-queue OS thread. Native failures remain typed errors; absent-format reads return empty text.
limits: Windows/Linux actual clipboard interoperation and availability failures still require target-host acceptance.
